title: Project management
description: Map dependencies, ownership and decision dates before committing to delivery.
questions: Which dependency can block the next release, and who owns it?
What can the team deliver independently and in what order?
Who decides on scope, dates and accepted risks?

specialists.title: Delivery planning
specialists.focus: Find the longest chain of unfinished dependencies and compare the proposed sequence with a smaller increment the team can deliver independently.

specialists.title: Capacity and dependencies
specialists.focus: Check availability and handoff dates with the teams that own shared people, environments, vendors or approvals.

specialists.title: Governance and escalation
specialists.focus: Identify who can change scope, dates or staffing and when that person needs to decide to protect delivery.

evidence: Check the latest milestone plan and dated commitments. Identify the owner and predecessor for each item that can move the delivery date.
Compare estimates with recent delivery of similar work, available team capacity and commitments the teams have already made.
Read acceptance criteria and the dependency or risk register. Confirm when each external owner can accept a handoff.
challenge: Check whether tasks shown in parallel compete for the same people or environment.
Test the plan against one plausible delay on the longest unfinished dependency chain. State which date, scope or capacity decision it changes.
Separate a target date from a commitment. Flag dates that depend on an unconfirmed estimate, decision or vendor.
decision_criteria: Recommend the sequence that delivers an accepted increment within confirmed capacity and names an owner for each blocking dependency.
For each date-sensitive assumption, identify an owner and the date by which it must be confirmed or escalated.
If the scope, date and capacity cannot all hold, present the trade-off for the person who can change one of them.
